title: Policy validator sabotage matrix after hardening
method: The tree is copied, exactly one mutation is applied, and tools/ci/policy_validator.py runs against the copy. Each mutation below survived the previous version of the rules; the rule it defeated is named with it.

mutants.mutation: --filter 'Category!=Flaky' on the required RabbitMQ step, single quotes
mutants.whyItSurvived: the pattern allowed an optional double quote only, so a single quote skipped past it
mutants.fix: the rule matches the --filter switch itself, not a predicate spelling

mutants.whyItSurvived: only Category and TestCategory predicates were matched
mutants.fix: same rule; NUnit.Where, --settings and TestCaseFilter are covered as well

mutants.mutation: [Ignore("temporarily disabled")] on a due RabbitMQ case
mutants.whyItSurvived: no rule read the test sources, and run_test_category.py checked only total, executed and failed
mutants.fix: [Ignore] is rejected outright, the [Explicit] count per project is bound to the inventory, and run_test_category.py now rejects any not executed case the inventory does not name

mutants.mutation: docker/build-push-action@v6 with push: true in the pack job
mutants.whyItSurvived: the rule matched the literals 'docker push' and 'ghcr.io', which an action does not contain
mutants.fix: publishing actions, push: true, login actions and publish credentials are covered

mutants.mutation: if: github.repository == 'NoSuchOrg/NoSuchRepo' on the required RabbitMQ job
mutants.whyItSurvived: three historic guard literals were matched and job presence was checked, not reachability
mutants.fix: a required job may carry no job level condition at all; step level conditions are unaffected

mutants.mutation: RequireRunScopedCredentials() removed from the RabbitMQ set up fixture
mutants.whyItSurvived: the endpoint rule exempts the run-scoped helpers and never scans src/, so the guard was the only barrier and nothing bound it
mutants.fix: the guard is bound: it must name all five variables, fail the run rather than warn, run as a set up fixture and actually be called

residual: The historic localhost/guest defaults in RabbitMqTestHarness and RunScopedBroker are unchanged, because removing them would change behaviour for a consumer pointing the harness at their own broker, which is a public API decision and not a developer one. They are now unreachable in a required run by a bound guard instead of by an unbound one.
